author: Opus subagent writing as AI agents
status: Provisional model-authored judgments; not independent expert ground truth.

policies.goals_policy: Expected goals reflect communication outcomes requested in the brief, not every taxonomy goal associated with an expected technique.
policies.subjects_policy: subjects lists required useful subject words; not_subjects lists particular instruction, format, or mechanism words that should not become subject searches. Other sensible subject words are not penalized by these lists.
policies.techniques_policy: Expected techniques require a named mechanism or concrete descriptive evidence. A mood or generic style alone does not establish a mechanism. Explicitly negated techniques are excluded.

cases.text: slide 7 of a board deck on our merger: juxtaposition of a 1950s print shop and a modern room full of servers
cases.rationale: The mechanism is named outright and the two compared subjects are given; no separate outcome is requested.

cases.text: atmospheric perspective, mountain ridges, for the background of a meditation app onboarding screen
cases.rationale: Terse keyword query naming the technique; the meditation context sets mood but no outcome is stated.

cases.text: User wants repetition with interruption for a poster about getting noticed in a crowded job market. Something like a crowd of matching grey umbrellas and a single yellow one.
cases.rationale: Named mechanism plus an example of one odd unit in a repeated set; getting noticed asks for one thing to pull attention.

cases.text: proximity grouping - 3 people talking in a tight knot, 1 person standing apart. for a slide on onboarding remote hires who feel left out
cases.rationale: Named mechanism; the left-out hire asks the image to show who belongs and who is apart.

cases.text: Need a reference that uses selective focus: a barista's hands pouring milk into a cup, the cafe behind melting away. For a blog header.
cases.rationale: Named mechanism with matching description of a dissolving background; no further outcome requested.

cases.text: goal: show scale. a person standing at the foot of a dam wall. infographic header for a hydropower report
cases.rationale: The goal is named directly and a familiar small figure beside a far larger structure is concrete evidence of scale contrast.

cases.text: hero image for a landing page about a budgeting app; should feel steady and trustworthy. the whole left half should be plain sky so the headline can sit there, with a single small house on the right
cases.rationale: A half-frame of plain sky around one small subject is negative space, the subject pushed to one side is off-centre placement, and steadiness asks for calm.

cases.text: slide 4 of a pitch deck: show that our market is small today but will be far bigger later. maybe a seedling next to the full-grown tree it grows into
cases.rationale: The seedling stands in for the market and its size against the grown tree carries the growth claim, so both mechanisms and both outcomes are requested.

cases.text: The user says: "I want people to look at the red door first, everything else on the street is grey and washed out." It's for a poetry collection cover.
cases.rationale: A saturated red accent in a grey field is colour contrast; looking at it first is the one-subject attention goal (the book genre is not a requested outcome).

cases.text: website section for our hiking tours. want the trail to pull the viewer from the bottom corner up to the hut on the ridge
cases.rationale: A path that carries the eye to a distant subject is a leading line, and the requested viewing path is guiding the eye.

cases.text: poster for a jazz night: a saxophonist reduced to a solid black shape in front of an orange sunset, no face detail visible
cases.rationale: A featureless dark figure against a bright sky is a silhouette; no outcome beyond the look is asked for.

cases.text: email newsletter banner for a sleep supplement. only soft blues and greys, nothing loud, a bedroom at dawn
cases.rationale: Restricting the image to one cool colour family is a limited palette, and 'nothing loud' asks for a quiet result.

cases.text: about-page photo idea: the founder working at her bench, seen past the edges of an open workshop door so the door boxes her in, like you're peeking in
cases.rationale: The door edges enclosing the subject are a frame within a frame; the peeking feel is a mood of the frame, not a separate requested outcome.

cases.text: Need a background for a running app splash screen: a runner caught with both feet off the ground, streaks trailing behind them, should feel quick
cases.rationale: An airborne mid-stride pose with directional streaks are motion cues, and feeling quick is the movement goal.

cases.text: image for a LinkedIn post about how small habits pile up: thousands of identical paper clips laid in neat lines edge to edge
cases.rationale: Identical units at regular intervals across the picture are a pattern, used here to make accumulation of habits concrete; nothing breaks the pattern.

cases.text: hero for a luxury skincare page: a wet stone next to a glass bottle, really feel the difference between grainy rock and polished glass
cases.rationale: Grainy against polished surfaces is texture contrast; no further communication outcome is requested.

cases.text: slide about information overload, user wants something that leaves viewers a bit on edge: a desk buried in papers, framed so the pile spills past every edge of the picture
cases.rationale: The subject cut by all frame edges is tight cropping, and leaving viewers on edge asks for unease.

cases.text: Background art for a fantasy novel landing page. a castle on a far hill, forest in front, a river in the middle, mountains way behind. want it to feel like you could walk into it
cases.rationale: Explicit front, middle and back planes are layered depth, and walking into it asks for deep space.

cases.text: image for a museum exhibition ad: the gallery hall shot from dead centre, left wall and right wall matching like reflections, very formal and still
cases.rationale: Halves matching around a central axis is symmetry, and 'formal and still' asks for order and calm.

cases.text: cover of a quarterly report on supply chain risk. a lone worker caught in one shaft of light cutting through an otherwise pitch-black warehouse
cases.rationale: One bright lit area in surrounding darkness is light-dark contrast; the report topic does not state a requested outcome.

cases.text: a slide about disruption in insurance: a giraffe standing in a perfectly normal office cubicle. the oddness is the hook
cases.rationale: An animal in a setting where it does not belong is incongruity, and making the oddness the hook asks for surprise.

cases.text: Instagram carousel cover about mental health: a woman by a window, her eyes turned toward something beyond the edge of the photo, leaving the viewer curious
cases.rationale: A look aimed out of frame is gaze direction; curiosity about the unseen implies something beyond what is shown.

cases.text: for the 404 page of a design studio site: a puzzling picture where you see a vase first and then two faces
cases.rationale: A shape whose reading flips between vase and faces is figure-ground ambiguity, and the puzzle asks the viewer to look again.

cases.text: Banner for a cycling club: riders banking hard into a bend, with the road and horizon running corner to corner across the frame. make it feel like it's moving
cases.rationale: Corner-to-corner lines are diagonals and riders banked mid-turn are motion cues; feeling like it moves is the stated goal.

cases.text: data journalism piece on the wealth gap: a mansion and a tarp shelter on the same street, both equally prominent
cases.rationale: Two unlike subjects of equal weight set for comparison is juxtaposition, used to make inequality visible.

cases.text: the user asked for 'one of those photos where a hiker is a speck at the bottom of a massive glacier' for a climate keynote
cases.rationale: A familiar small figure against a vast form is scale contrast, and making the glacier read as vast is the scale goal.

cases.text: header image for a winter newsletter: snowy field, nothing in it except one red barn far off to the right
cases.rationale: A single subject in an otherwise empty field is negative space and its placement to one side is off-centre balance; red on white is not a hue contrast, and no outcome is stated.

cases.text: slide for a talk on privacy: a hand held over a face, the hand shaped like a padlock
cases.rationale: A hand fused with a padlock transfers the meaning of locking to the face, expressing privacy through a concrete form.

cases.text: app store screenshot background for a birdwatching app: starlings bunched tightly on the left of the wire, one starling sitting alone way over on the right
cases.rationale: Spacing alone separates one bird from the cluster, which is proximity grouping showing belonging and separation.

cases.text: keynote opener on seeing the whole system: a city intersection shot from a drone pointing straight at the ground, crosswalks and cars flattened into a graphic
cases.rationale: A straight-down camera position is an unusual vantage point; the theme title does not itself request a separate outcome.

cases.text: Hero for a farm-to-table restaurant site: vegetables laid out in neat repeating lines in market crates. NOT a shallow-focus shot, the user wants everything sharp.
cases.rationale: Selective focus is explicitly rejected; regular repeated lines of produce still establish pattern.

cases.text: poster for a chamber orchestra. no silhouettes, the user wants faces visible. violinists on stage lit hard from one side with the rest of the stage black
cases.rationale: Silhouette is negated; lit, modelled figures in surrounding darkness are light-dark contrast.

cases.text: landing page for a co-working space; avoid anything mirror-balanced or centred. put a lone desk off to the left with daylight coming through the window
cases.rationale: Symmetry is explicitly excluded; the subject placed to one side is off-centre placement.

cases.text: slide on product reliability: a lighthouse in a storm, but no canted or skewed framing, keep the horizon level and upright
cases.rationale: Diagonal energy is rejected and nothing else describes a mechanism; a storm alone does not establish one.

cases.text: cover for a report on urban heat islands
cases.rationale: Topic only; no composition or outcome is described.

cases.text: blog post thumbnail: sourdough bread
cases.rationale: A format and a subject; nothing establishes a mechanism.

cases.text: illustration for a chapter on the history of the printing press. user just said 'something old-timey and warm'
cases.rationale: Period feel and warmth are mood words that do not name a palette, layout or other mechanism.

cases.text: beekeeping, hives, summer
cases.rationale: Bare keywords give subjects only.

cases.text: user's words: 'make it feel hopeful'. it's the closing slide of a fundraising deck for a children's hospital
cases.rationale: Hopefulness is a mood with no matching codebook goal or mechanism, and no visual description is given.

cases.text: og:image for a blog post about remote work in Lisbon
cases.rationale: Place and topic only; no mechanism or outcome.
